citation: Witte Paz M, Harbig TA, Nieselt K. Evidente—a visual analytics tool for data enrichment in SNP-based phylogenetic trees. Bioinformatics Advances. 2022.
evidence_note: Primary paper introduces Evidente and its CLASSICO module. CLASSICO computes SNP clade-specificity by propagating alleles through the tree and labels SNPs occurring only in one clade as clade-specific/supporting.

citation: Edwards DJ, Duchene S, Pope B, Holt KE. SNPPar: identifying convergent evolution and other homoplasies from microbial whole-genome alignments. Microbial Genomics. 2021.
evidence_note: Primary paper describes SNPPar software and source code. SNPPar assigns mutation events to branches and reports precise ancestral-to-derived base substitutions and branches.

citation: Monit C, Goldstein RA. SubRecon: ancestral reconstruction of amino acid substitutions along a branch in a phylogeny. Bioinformatics. 2018.
evidence_note: Primary paper presents SubRecon and source-code availability. It calculates joint probabilities of states at adjacent internal nodes and explicitly reconstructs how state changed along a branch.

citation: Sagulenko P, Puller V, Neher RA. TreeTime: Maximum-likelihood phylodynamic analysis. Virus Evolution. 2018.
evidence_note: Primary paper presents the Python TreeTime framework, including ancestral-state inference. This distinguishes the intended tool from an unrelated 2009 C++ program with the same name.

citation: TreeTime documentation, ancestral sequence reconstruction / ancestral command.
evidence_note: Official documentation states that the ancestral command reconstructs ancestral sequences and maps mutations to the tree; the annotated Nexus output contains mutations on branches.

citation: Ashkenazy H et al. FastML: a web server for probabilistic reconstruction of ancestral sequences. Nucleic Acids Research. 2012.
evidence_note: FastML reconstructs ancestral nucleotide, amino-acid or codon sequences at internal phylogenetic nodes. Its documented first-class output is ancestral sequence/state reconstruction rather than an explicit branch-change endpoint.

citation: Gardner SN, Slezak T, Hall BG. kSNP3.0: SNP detection and phylogenetic analysis of genomes without genome alignment or reference genome. Bioinformatics. 2015.
evidence_note: Primary paper establishes kSNP3.0 as a significantly improved version of kSNP v2 and documents stand-alone software. The kSNP lineage reports SNPs unique to tree nodes and includes utilities to obtain SNP loci mapped to a node. Node-associated SNP output is near-direct under the frozen rubric.

citation: Yang Z. PAML 4: phylogenetic analysis by maximum likelihood. Molecular Biology and Evolution. 2007.
evidence_note: Primary publication describes the PAML software package and ancestral gene/protein reconstruction. Ancestral reconstruction is a first-class output, but the cited source does not establish BRANCHSNV D1 or D2 as the direct output.

citation: Ishikawa SA, Zhukova A, Iwasaki W, Gascuel O. A Fast Likelihood Method to Reconstruct and Visualize Ancestral Scenarios. Molecular Biology and Evolution. 2019.
evidence_note: Primary publication presents PastML software for ancestral character reconstruction. It predicts ancestral states at nodes and visualizes ancestral scenarios; this is near-direct under the frozen rubric.
